references.text: Isaac's eyes were weak so that he could not see, which explains why he had to feel his son to identify him.
Jacob enters Isaac and pretends to be Esau, setting the stage for Isaac's doubt in verse 21.
Isaac feels Jacob and becomes confused—the voice is Jacob's, but the hands are Esau's—directly following up on his desire to verify in verse 21.
The background of the conflict: Esau sold his birthright to Jacob, which motivated Jacob's desire to secure the blessing.
The consequences of Jacob's deception: Esau discovers that the blessing has been stolen and describes Jacob's betrayal.
Both verses document Isaac's attempt to verify his son's identity during the deception, where 27:32 shows the consequence of the doubt expressed in 27:21.
Contrasting moments in the same event: 27:21 shows Isaac's doubt before the blessing, while 27:37 shows his resignation after it has been completed.
